info.title: ai-raccoon
info.description: An MCP server that gives AI agents persistent, project-scoped memory: a memory bank over sqlite-memory with hybrid vector+BM25 search, workspace sandboxes, a shared promotion tier, and optional S3/Azure sync.

x-inspectra.cliParsedDescription: MCP server exposing agent memory over sqlite-memory

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Shows the bank schema/version, code engine state, and embedding settings without changing the bank. Use this when a bank looks mismatched or a search result feels wrong.

commands.name: encryption
commands.description: Bank encryption source configuration

commands.name: bitwarden
commands.description: Configures Bitwarden Secrets Manager as the bank key source (interactive ids; rekeys the bank)

options.name: -t
options.description: access token for this run only — never persisted; defaults to BWS_ACCESS_TOKEN

commands.name: list
commands.description: Shows the current encryption source

commands.name: migrate
commands.description: Rekeys a bank still encrypted under the old key derivation

commands.name: remove
commands.description: Returns to the env default (rekeys the bank when AIRACCOON_DB_PASSPHRASE is set)

commands.name: extract
commands.description: Shared-extraction operations. The service is CONFIGURED under 'settings extract'.

commands.name: prune
commands.description: Reports promotion_queue rows whose backing entry is gone. Reports per-project counts by default; --apply removes them. Idempotent.

options.name: --apply
options.description: Removes the orphaned rows instead of only reporting them

commands.name: model
commands.description: Embedding engine selection (for memory embeddings or code corpus); configuration is under 'settings model'

commands.name: code
commands.description: Code corpus embedding engine (local only in v1); configuration is under 'settings model code'

commands.name: set
commands.description: Activates a model for the code corpus

commands.name: download
commands.description: Downloads a Hugging Face embedding model into <data-root>/models/<slug> with SHA-256 pins. Does NOT activate — 'model embedding set local <dir>' or 'model code set local <dir>' is the next step.

options.name: --file
options.description: Download this repo-relative file instead of auto-selecting onnx/model.onnx (repeatable; external-data siblings are still enumerated)

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Resolve and print files, sizes and SHA-256 pins without downloading anything

options.name: --yes
options.description: Skip the size confirmation for downloads larger than 500 MB

commands.name: embedding
commands.description: Memory bank embedding engine; configuration is under 'settings model embedding'

commands.name: set
commands.description: Sets the memory embedding engine and re-embeds the bank. Blocks all reads and writes until done — minutes on a large bank

commands.name: local
commands.description: Embeds in-process with the bundled ONNX model; optional path overrides it

commands.name: openai
commands.description: Routes through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint; key via --api-key (persisted in settings)

options.name: --api-key
options.description: API key persisted in the settings table

options.name: --dims
options.description: Output dimension the endpoint returns (sqlite-vec cannot infer it)

commands.name: noise
commands.description: Rejected-write training data. Rejection is CONFIGURED under 'settings noise'.

commands.name: entries
commands.description: Summarizes noise_entries — the training-data source for a future noise learner

commands.name: repair
commands.description: Fixes bank-state drift by asking the server to repair it. chunk-index fixes wrong chunk positions; reingest re-processes files a chunker change made unreproducible; project-ids folds fragment ids into one.

commands.name: chunk-index
commands.description: Use this when chunk positions drifted from document order. Reports by default; --apply asks the server to fix them.

options.name: --apply
options.description: Ask the server to fix the positions on its next maintenance poll (~15s)

commands.name: project-ids
commands.description: Use this when several project ids name the same project. Diagnoses by default; --apply asks the server to fold them.

options.name: --apply
options.description: Ask the server to fold the ids on its next maintenance poll (~15s)

options.name: --diagnose
options.description: Show the id clusters without queueing anything (the default)

commands.name: reingest
commands.description: Use this when a chunker change makes stored chunks unreproducible. Reports by default; --apply asks the server to re-ingest them.

options.name: --apply
options.description: Ask the server to re-ingest the files on its next maintenance poll (~15s)

commands.name: serve
commands.description: Serves the MCP endpoint over HTTP (always HTTP). Background it: ai-raccoon serve > serve.log 2>&1 &

options.name: --port
options.description: HTTP port to bind; 0 picks a random free port [default: 7721]

options.name: --mcp-entry
options.description: Print the MCP client config entry for the bound URL

options.name: --restart
options.description: Stop the ai-raccoon server already on the port and serve in its place (a plain start when none is)

commands.name: observability
commands.description: Prints a ready-to-run monitoring command for the live server, with its PID filled in

options.name: --port
options.description: Port of the running serve process to query [default: 7721]

commands.name: settings
commands.description: Runtime configuration, one node per subsystem. Operations live at the top level: 'watch registered', 'extract prune', 'noise entries', 'model embedding set', 'model code set', 'encryption', 'serve'.

commands.name: access
commands.description: Access-mode configuration (per-project overrides the global default)

commands.name: default
commands.description: Global default access mode

commands.name: set
commands.description: Sets the global default

commands.name: show
commands.description: Shows the effective global default (row value, else rw)

commands.name: list
commands.description: Lists the default and every override

commands.name: set
commands.description: Sets a per-project override; '*' targets the global default

commands.name: unset
commands.description: Drops a per-project override (falls back to the default)

commands.name: extract
commands.description: Background shared-extraction configuration: enables or disables the hosted service that periodically checks each project's committed memories and extracts the shared-worthy ones, and sets its mode (propose logs candidates; promote shares them).

commands.name: auto-promote-threshold
commands.description: Sets the score-gated auto-promote threshold (0..4, e.g. 3.5) or 'off' (default): in promote mode, queued candidates scoring at or above share automatically and nothing below is queued

commands.name: capacity
commands.description: Sets the propose-tier queue capacity (positive integer; default 1000) — the total queued candidates across projects, split into per-project reservations

commands.name: enable
commands.description: Enables or disables the background shared-extraction service (disabled by default; promote mode shares data between projects)

commands.name: exclude
commands.description: Excludes source_file prefixes from shared-extraction candidacy (extract.exclude.prefixes; e.g. 'scratch/' keeps agent scratch files out of the shared tier)

commands.name: add
commands.description: Adds a source_file prefix to the exclusion list (deduped)

commands.name: list
commands.description: Lists the excluded source_file prefixes

commands.name: remove
commands.description: Removes a source_file prefix from the exclusion list

commands.name: interval
commands.description: Sets the extraction pass interval in minutes (positive integer; default 30)

commands.name: list
commands.description: Shows the extraction configuration (enabled, mode, interval minutes)

commands.name: mode
commands.description: Sets the extraction mode: propose (default, logs ranked candidates) or promote (shares the top candidates into the shared tier)

commands.name: ingest
commands.description: Ingestion configuration. The scope allowlist bounds every path the server reads from disk — memory_ingest_file, memory_ingest_directory, memory_watch_add and the file watcher. It is empty by default, so a project ingests nothing until a scope is added.

commands.name: scope
commands.description: Scope allowlist (absolute paths, covers dir + subdirs) — the paths this server may read

commands.name: add
commands.description: Adds a scope path (normalized absolute, deduped, re-sorted)

commands.name: list
commands.description: Lists a target's scope allowlist

commands.name: remove
commands.description: Removes a scope path

commands.name: maintenance
commands.description: Bank maintenance configuration (CLI-only channel): the checkpoint interval bounds the WAL — every process runs wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) at startup and shutdown, and the periodic timer on this cadence — and the vacuum interval sets how often VACUUM + ANALYZE run (per-process clock; short-lived processes never vacuum).

commands.name: embed-rows-per-run
commands.description: Sets the embed drain's rows-per-signal, for both corpora (positive integer; default 128) — takes effect on the drain's next pass, no restart

commands.name: interval
commands.description: Sets the WAL checkpoint interval in minutes (positive integer; default 60)

commands.name: list
commands.description: Shows the bank maintenance configuration (checkpoint interval, vacuum interval, embed rows per run)

commands.name: vacuum-interval
commands.description: Sets the VACUUM + ANALYZE interval in days (positive integer; default 7)

commands.name: model
commands.description: Embedding engine configuration (the engine itself is selected by 'model embedding set' or 'model code set')

commands.name: code
commands.description: Code corpus embedding engine configuration (the engine itself is selected by 'model code set local')

commands.name: list
commands.description: Shows the configured code corpus model and engine

commands.name: remove
commands.description: Deletes ONLY the code engine rows (embedding.codeModel/codeEngine) — the memory engine is untouched

commands.name: embedding
commands.description: Memory bank embedding engine configuration

commands.name: list
commands.description: Shows the configured memory embedding provider/model/baseUrl/dims

commands.name: remove
commands.description: Back to default: no engine (FTS5-only search). Never touches the code engine's rows — see 'settings model code reset'.

commands.name: list
commands.description: Shows the configured provider/model/baseUrl/engine, and the code engine rows when set

commands.name: remove
commands.description: Back to default: no engine (FTS5-only search). Never touches the code engine's rows — see 'settings model code reset'.

commands.name: threads
commands.description: ORT intra-op thread cap for local embedding sessions (0 = ORT default, unset = max(1, logicalCores/2)). Takes effect on the next server restart — sessions are cached per engine fingerprint.

commands.name: noise
commands.description: Pre-write noise rejection: the kill switch for the deterministic Hermes background-process-log filter. Rejection is ON by default — 'noise disable' is how you disarm it. Entries the filter rejected are read via 'noise entries', not here — that reads the noise_entries data table, not settings.

commands.name: disable
commands.description: Disarms pre-write noise rejection — every write is stored, even ones a policy would otherwise refuse

commands.name: enable
commands.description: Arms pre-write noise rejection (the default)

commands.name: list
commands.description: Shows whether pre-write noise rejection is enabled

commands.name: performance
commands.description: Metrics subsystem configuration (CLI-only channel): buffer capacity and flush interval tune the background writer, hot-table retention tunes the reaper. Each takes effect on a different cadence — buffer capacity on the next server restart, flush interval on the next flush tick, retention on the next maintenance pass — every command below states its own.

commands.name: buffer-capacity
commands.description: Sets the measurement buffer capacity (positive integer, max 1000000; default 1000) — takes effect on the next server restart

commands.name: flush-interval
commands.description: Sets the metrics flush interval in seconds (positive integer; default 30) — takes effect on the next flush tick

commands.name: list
commands.description: Shows the metrics subsystem configuration (buffer capacity, flush interval, retention)

commands.name: retention
commands.description: Sets the hot metrics-table retention in days (positive integer, max 36500; default 28) — takes effect on the next maintenance pass

commands.name: queryguard
commands.description: Read-path query guard: refuses a memory_search query that is itself machine output (e.g. a pasted background-process notification) and annotates one that merely contains log-like content. Armed by default — 'queryguard disable' is how you disarm it.

commands.name: disable
commands.description: Disarms the read-path query guard — every query runs untouched, even ones a policy would otherwise refuse or annotate

commands.name: enable
commands.description: Arms the read-path query guard (the default)

commands.name: list
commands.description: Shows whether the guard, shadow mode and the structural detector are enabled

commands.name: shadow
commands.description: Shadow mode: records what the guard would have done without refusing or annotating anything — measure real traffic before enabling

commands.name: disable
commands.description: Disarms shadow mode (the default): the guard acts on its verdicts

commands.name: enable
commands.description: Arms shadow mode (off by default)

commands.name: structural
commands.description: Structural detector: a learned, vocabulary-free third input to the warn tier. Off by default — it only ever adds an annotation, never a refusal.

commands.name: disable
commands.description: Disarms the structural detector (the default)

commands.name: enable
commands.description: Arms the structural detector

commands.name: threshold
commands.description: Score a query must clear before the detector annotates it

commands.name: set
commands.description: Sets queryGuard.structural.threshold (0..1)

commands.name: retrieval
commands.description: Retrieval configuration

commands.name: alpha
commands.description: Dual-vector fusion alpha

commands.name: set
commands.description: Sets retrieval.structureAlpha (0..1, default 0.5)

commands.name: show
commands.description: Shows the current alpha (row value, else 0.5)

commands.name: consolidation
commands.description: Sets retrieval.consolidationThreshold (>= 0, default 0.1)

commands.name: set
commands.description: Sets retrieval.consolidationThreshold (>= 0, default 0.1)

commands.name: show
commands.description: Shows the current retrieval.consolidationThreshold (row value, else 0.1)

commands.name: doc-formula
commands.description: Sets retrieval.docScoreFormula (max|sum, default max)

commands.name: set
commands.description: Sets retrieval.docScoreFormula (max|sum, default max)

commands.name: show
commands.description: Shows the current retrieval.docScoreFormula (row value, else max)

commands.name: fts-weight
commands.description: Sets retrieval.ftsWeight (integer >= 0, default 1)

commands.name: set
commands.description: Sets retrieval.ftsWeight (integer >= 0, default 1)

commands.name: show
commands.description: Shows the current retrieval.ftsWeight (row value, else 1)

commands.name: fusion
commands.description: No-fusion-regression reorder: keeps a result from ranking below where its best single modality put it. OFF by default — 'fusion enable' arms it and starts recording how it differs from the baseline.

commands.name: disable
commands.description: Back to the baseline fusion (the default)

commands.name: enable
commands.description: Arms the reorder and its evidence collection (not the default)

commands.name: list
commands.description: Shows whether the reorder is armed, and names the default

commands.name: rrfk
commands.description: Sets retrieval.rrfK (integer >= 1, default 60)

commands.name: set
commands.description: Sets retrieval.rrfK (integer >= 1, default 60)

commands.name: show
commands.description: Shows the current retrieval.rrfK (row value, else 60)

commands.name: show-all
commands.description: Shows every retrieval option with its source (setting or default)

commands.name: source-lambda
commands.description: Sets retrieval.sourceLambda (0..1, default 0.1)

commands.name: set
commands.description: Sets retrieval.sourceLambda (0..1, default 0.1)

commands.name: show
commands.description: Shows the current retrieval.sourceLambda (row value, else 0.1)

commands.name: vector-weight
commands.description: Sets retrieval.vectorWeight (integer >= 0, default 1)

commands.name: set
commands.description: Sets retrieval.vectorWeight (integer >= 0, default 1)

commands.name: show
commands.description: Shows the current retrieval.vectorWeight (row value, else 1)

commands.name: window
commands.description: Sets retrieval.candidateWindow (max3x100|max5x50, default max3x100)

commands.name: set
commands.description: Sets retrieval.candidateWindow (max3x100|max5x50, default max3x100)

commands.name: show
commands.description: Shows the current retrieval.candidateWindow (row value, else max3x100)

commands.name: sweep
commands.description: Background reaper configuration: the kill switch, the cadence and the rating threshold it deletes below. The reaper is ON by default — 'sweep disable' is how you disarm it. Per-entry TTLs are data, set by the memory_set_ttl tool, not configured here.

commands.name: disable
commands.description: Disarms the background reaper — nothing is deleted until it is enabled again

commands.name: enable
commands.description: Arms the background reaper (the default: it deletes expired entries on its cadence)

commands.name: interval-hours
commands.description: Sets the reaper cadence in hours (1..8760, default 24); applies live, no server restart needed

commands.name: list
commands.description: Shows the whole policy: enabled, interval hours and threshold (row values, else the defaults)

commands.name: threshold
commands.description: Sweep rating threshold

commands.name: set
commands.description: Sets sweep.threshold (0..1, default 0.3)

commands.name: sync
commands.description: Cloud sync configuration

commands.name: add
commands.description: Adds cloud sync

commands.name: azure
commands.description: Azure Blob container (connection string prompted, or --cli with DefaultAzureCredential)

options.name: --cli
options.description: Use DefaultAzureCredential (az login); no connection-string prompt

commands.name: s3
commands.description: S3-compatible endpoint (credentials are persisted in the settings table, or use --cli for the AWS credential chain)

options.name: --cli
options.description: Use the AWS default credential chain (aws configure / aws sso login); no key prompts

commands.name: list
commands.description: Shows the sync configuration (keys redacted)

commands.name: remove
commands.description: Back to default: sync off

commands.name: watch
commands.description: Watch configuration: enable/disable and concurrency per target. This node CONFIGURES watching — it does not register watches; use 'watch registered' to list registrations.

commands.name: concurrency
commands.description: Sets the watcher concurrency (1..16, default 4)

commands.name: disable
commands.description: Alias for enable … false

commands.name: enable
commands.description: Enables or disables watching for a target (configuration only — does not register a watch; use memory_watch_add to register)

commands.name: list
commands.description: Lists each target's watch CONFIGURATION (enabled, concurrency, scope) — not registered watches; use 'watch registered' for those

commands.name: remove
commands.description: Removes all watch config rows for a target

commands.name: watch
commands.description: Registered watches. Watching is CONFIGURED under 'settings watch'; registrations are created by agents via the memory_watch_add MCP tool.

commands.name: registered
commands.description: Lists every REGISTERED watch (project, path, registered at, last change) from the watches table. Registrations are created via memory_watch_add; live state (scanning/healthy/…) is reported by memory_watch_status, not the CLI.

options.name: --transport
options.description: MCP transport; proxy (default) relays to one HTTP backend, https unsupported

options.name: --data-root
options.description: Bank data root (must precede the verb)

options.name: --quiet
options.description: Quiet mode: every log level goes to a file beside the bank, nothing reaches stdout/stderr

options.name: --port
options.description: HTTP backend port the proxy dials or starts (1-65535); 0 is serve-only [default: 7721]
